title: Advance Beneficiary Notice Settings by Tier — Outpatient and Part B Therapy Services
content:
The Advance Beneficiary Notice of Non-coverage (form CMS-R-131) is set tier by tier for **Outpatient and Part B Therapy Services** as follows.

| Tier | ABN must be delivered before a service Medicare is expected to deny is billed to the resident | Choices printed on the ABN | Resident may be billed for a denied service when no valid ABN was delivered |
|---|---|---|---|
| Medicare Part B Physical Therapy Plan of Care | Yes | Option 1, bill Medicare; Option 2, do not bill; Option 3, decline the service | No |
| Medicare Part B Occupational Therapy Plan of Care | Yes | Option 1, bill Medicare; Option 2, do not bill; Option 3, decline the service | No |
| Medicare Part B Speech-Language Pathology Plan of Care | Yes | Option 1, bill Medicare; Option 2, do not bill; Option 3, decline the service | No |
| Medicare Advantage Outpatient Therapy Plan of Care | No | Option 1, bill Medicare; Option 2, do not bill; Option 3, decline the service | No |
| Medical Assistance Therapy Plan of Care | No | Option 1, bill Medicare; Option 2, do not bill; Option 3, decline the service | No |
| Private Pay Therapy Plan of Care | No | Option 1, bill Medicare; Option 2, do not bill; Option 3, decline the service | No |

## The settings in words

- In the three Medicare Part B tiers, the ABN must be delivered before a service Medicare is expected to deny is billed to the resident. In the Medicare Advantage, Medical Assistance and Private Pay tiers this setting is No.
- The ABN prints three controlled choices: Option 1 (bill Medicare), Option 2 (do not bill) and Option 3 (decline the service). Exactly these three are the choices of the notice.
- In every tier, when no valid ABN was delivered, the resident may not be billed for a denied service.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical cases)

| Hypothetical case | Reading under these settings |
|---|---|
| A Part B physical therapy service Medicare denied; a valid ABN was not delivered | The resident may not be billed for it |
| A Part B occupational therapy plan; Medicare is expected to deny a service the resident wishes to receive | The ABN must be delivered before that service is billed to the resident |
